statement: Let out be the returned value. For a cell index i define covered(i) to mean: 0 <= i < n and there exists j with 0 <= j < len(ranges) and ranges[j][0] <= i <= ranges[j][1]. Define uncovered(i) to mean: 0 <= i < n and not covered(i). Then all of the following hold. (a) For every k with 0 <= k < len(out): len(out[k]) = 2, 0 <= out[k][0] <= out[k][1] < n, every i with out[k][0] <= i <= out[k][1] is uncovered, and (out[k][0] = 0 or covered(out[k][0]-1)) and (out[k][1] = n-1 or covered(out[k][1]+1)). (b) The intervals are strictly increasing in start: for every k with 0 <= k < len(out)-1, out[k][0] < out[k+1][0]. (c) Conversely, for every pair a,b with 0 <= a <= b < n such that every i with a <= i <= b is uncovered, and such that (a = 0 or covered(a-1)) and (b = n-1 or covered(b+1)), there is exactly one k with out[k][0] = a and out[k][1] = b.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered, so a range ending at n covers up to n-1.)

statement: For the returned out, every k with 0 <= k < len(out) satisfies 0 <= out[k][0] <= out[k][1] <= n-1.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered.)

statement: For the returned out, every k with 0 <= k < len(out) satisfies len(out[k]) = 2.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered.)

statement: For the returned out, for every k with 0 <= k < len(out) and every i with out[k][0] <= i <= out[k][1]: there is no j with 0 <= j < len(ranges) and ranges[j][0] <= i <= ranges[j][1] (that is, cell i is uncovered).
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered.)

statement: For the returned out, for every k with 0 <= k < len(out): either out[k][0] = 0, or there exists j with 0 <= j < len(ranges) and ranges[j][0] <= out[k][0]-1 <= ranges[j][1].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered.)

statement: For the returned out, for every k with 0 <= k < len(out): either out[k][1] = n-1, or there exists j with 0 <= j < len(ranges) and ranges[j][0] <= out[k][1]+1 <= ranges[j][1].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered.)

statement: For the returned out, for every i with 0 <= i < n such that there is no j with 0 <= j < len(ranges) and ranges[j][0] <= i <= ranges[j][1] (i.e., cell i is uncovered): there exists k with 0 <= k < len(out) and out[k][0] <= i <= out[k][1].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered.)

statement: For the returned out, and for any two distinct indices k, m with 0 <= k < len(out) and 0 <= m < len(out), the intervals [out[k][0], out[k][1]] and [out[m][0], out[m][1]] are disjoint: there is no integer i with out[k][0] <= i <= out[k][1] and out[m][0] <= i <= out[m][1].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. statement: For the returned out, for every k with 0 <= k < len(out)-1: out[k][0] < out[k+1][0].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. statement: For the returned out, for every k with 0 <= k < len(out)-1: out[k][1] + 1 < out[k+1][0].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. statement: For the returned out: len(out) = 0 if and only if every i with 0 <= i < n is covered, i.e., for every i with 0 <= i < n there exists j with 0 <= j < len(ranges) and ranges[j][0] <= i <= ranges[j][1].
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered.)

statement: The function returns Ok r for some value r on every input satisfying the preconditions; it never fails (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic occurs).
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; all computed bounds such as ranges[j][1]+1 and out[k][1]+1 are then at most 10^9+1, within i64.)

statement: Suppose there is at least one uncovered cell, i.e., some i with 0 <= i < n such that no j with 0 <= j < len(ranges) has ranges[j][0] <= i <= ranges[j][1]. Then for the returned out: len(out) >= 1, out[0][0] equals the least uncovered cell index, and out[len(out)-1][1] equals the greatest uncovered cell index.
preconditions: 1 <= n <= 10^9; 0 <= len(ranges) <= 10^6; for every j with 0 <= j < len(ranges): len(ranges[j]) = 2, 0 <= ranges[j][0] <= n-1, and ranges[j][0] <= ranges[j][1] <= n. (The upper bound n on ranges[j][1], rather than n-1, is required by the example n = 10^9, ranges = [[0,10^9]]; only cells 0..n-1 are considered.)
